artifacts.summary: Re-verified both defect halves (broken lake-build-guard.sh --module vectors; hardcoded Theories/ scan root that silently passes when missing/empty) against the current source tree post-task-221/173, with exact current line numbers, mechanical confirmation of the exit-0-on-empty bug in lean-sorry-census.sh, and real lakefile.toml evidence from BimodalLogic and cslib supporting a lakefile-derived resolver design.

memory_candidates.content: When a taught verification snippet's failure mode is 'silently passes on empty/missing input' (e.g. a grep or census over a directory that doesn't exist in this consuming repo), confirm the exact silent-pass mechanism by reading the script's own code path (e.g. lean-sorry-census.sh's `if [[ ${#LEAN_FILES[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then echo sorry_count: 0; exit 0; fi`) rather than only inferring it from the reported symptom. This turns a hypothesis into a mechanically-verified defect and pins the exact line(s) to fix.

For Lean/Lake consuming repos, source roots are derivable from lakefile.toml's [[lean_lib]] entries applying Lake's own defaults (srcDir default '.', roots default [name]) rather than hardcoding a literal directory name. A working precedent already exists in ~/Projects/BimodalLogic/scripts/lake_targets.py (stdlib tomllib, exits 2 with a stderr message naming the failure on a missing/unparseable lakefile or absent target) -- useful design grounding for any agent-system resolver needing per-repo Lean source roots, though that script itself is project-local and not reusable directly from the source store.
